NYPD told CBS that facial recognition was used only as a possible lead and that an arrest would not be made solely from a facial-recognition match.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Legal Aid reports from its review of NYPD records that FIS first returned no match for surveillance material in a public-lewdness investigation; hours later a possible match was entered that Legal Aid says came from the Special Activities Unit rather than FIS. Legal Aid states that the later match identified Trevis Williams even though he did not match the victim's physical description, and that the match was followed by an identification procedure and arrest. CBS independently reports that Williams spent more than two days in custody, was charged with indecent exposure and that the case was later dismissed. Williams told CBS that the experience remained very stressful and that he continued to think about the possibility that he could have been required to register as a sex offender. Legal Aid also states that his life and job prospects were put on hold. NYPD told CBS that facial recognition was only a possible lead and that the arrest was not made solely on the match.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: This occurrence combines inferential-authority risk with a material provenance discontinuity. An initial no-match did not end the inquiry; a different unit later produced a possible match whose method, database and approval basis remain unclear in the public record. That later inference selected Williams for a downstream identification pathway despite a material mismatch with the victim's description. Legal Aid disputes the independence and adequacy of the later identification procedure, while NYPD states that the victim identification and other investigative information contributed to probable cause. The preserved evidence therefore supports an affirmative Inferential Evidence–Authority Separation boundary finding rather than a failure occurrence. The invariant remains that a probabilistic identity inference must stay provisional until the downstream evidentiary basis and contradictory checks are sufficient for the contemplated coercive effect. The preserved competing accounts leave the independence and sufficiency of downstream identification unresolved; they support the existing ambiguous boundaries, without proving either an inference-only arrest or an invariant success. The OECD challenge-information benchmark engages this consequential biometric pathway, but the public record lacks the information supplied to Williams for challenging the AI result, so its finding remains evidence-insufficient. Other candidates are temporally or materially excluded or retain unresolved implementation and conformance scope. Dismissal does not resolve the contested policy or liability claims.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This incident demonstrates that contestability requires both evidentiary independence and provenance. A consequential identity inference should carry enough lineage to show which unit generated it, against what authorised source set, by what method and under what approval, especially when it contradicts an earlier search. Decision-makers should also be required to document which downstream evidence arose independently of the machine nomination and which contradictions were actively resolved before arrest or detention.
